title: Spring Data MongoDB
summary: Connect Spring Boot to MongoDB and choose the right persistence model.

richText: MongoDB stores documents. A document contains named fields and values, including nested objects and arrays.
BSON is MongoDB’s stored document format. It supports types such as dates and ObjectId in addition to JSON values.
A collection groups documents. The journal example uses journal_entries for entries and users for users.
Each document has an _id. ObjectId is one possible identifier type. Use the same Java ID type in the document and its repository.
Flexible document structure does not remove validation requirements. Validate incoming data before saving it.
Add spring-boot-starter-data-mongodb for blocking MongoDB access. Let the Spring Boot parent or BOM manage its dependency version.
BOM means bill of materials. It selects compatible dependency versions for the chosen Spring Boot release.
Spring Boot configures the MongoDB client, MongoTemplate and repository support when the dependencies and settings are available.
Use a local MongoDB instance for local learning, or Atlas for a managed MongoDB deployment. Atlas still requires a database user and permitted network access.
Keep the full connection URI in the MONGODB_URI environment variable. Include the intended database in that URI. Do not commit database credentials.
These additions use Spring Boot 3 and Java 17. The course repository uses Spring Boot 2.7.16 and Java 8. Match documentation and dependency versions to your project.
A connection failure can come from the URI, authentication, network access or an unavailable server. Adding a starter alone does not prove the database connection works.
Choose MongoDB when your data and read patterns fit documents. Choose a relational database when your design depends on relational constraints and joins.
